samples.summary: mergeSelection now persists the merge before clearing covered cells, so a throw mid-clear flushes a merge the sheet does not know about
samples.evidence: `mergeSelection` moved `await this.store.setMerge(anchor, span)` to line 4929, ahead of the cell-clearing loop (4931-4943) and ahead of `this.merges.set(...)` (4945). With `YorkieStore`, `setMerge` queues its write into `batchOps`, and `endBatch()` in the `finally` (4952) flushes `batchOps` unconditionally (yorkie-store.ts:1263-1267) — there is no rollback. If anything between 4931 and 4950 rejects (a `store.get`/`store.set`/`store.delete` on the CRDT, or `calculate`), the document ends up holding the merged block while the in-memory `this.merges` map never got the entry and the covered cells were only partly cleared: the local view shows no merge, the persisted sheet hides cell content under one, and the two disagree until reload. Before this change the same throw aborted before `setMerge`, so no merge was written. The ordering is deliberate (so a refusal costs nothing), but it trades a no-write failure mode for a half-written one.

samples.summary: A store refusal makes the merge gesture a silent no-op that repeats forever, because the engine never refreshes its merge budget from the store
samples.evidence: `mergeSelection` returns `false` when `store.setMerge` refuses (4929) but leaves `this.merges`/`this.mergeBudget` untouched, so `canMergeSelection()` (4874-4893), which budgets only the local `this.mergeBudget` (4891), keeps answering `true`. The toolbar therefore stays enabled and every subsequent click is another silent no-op with no user-visible reason and no re-read of the store's map (`this.merges = await this.store.getMerges()` happens only in load, sheet.ts:589). The refusal path the change exists to handle therefore terminates in an unexplained dead button rather than a corrected local view.

samples.summary: projectedMerges ignores batched shiftCells/moveCells ops, which rewrite ws.merges wholesale, so a batch mixing them with setMerge/deleteMerge budgets against stale anchors
samples.evidence: `projectedMerges()` (975-991) overlays only `batchMerges`, which is written solely by `setMerge`/`deleteMerge`. But `shiftCells` (484-508) and `moveCells` (510-539) also push ops into the same `batchOps`, and those ops call `applyWorksheetShift`/`applyWorksheetMove`, which replace the whole merge map via `replaceMerges` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:363-368). Inside such a batch, both the budget in `setMerge` (1014-1021) and the existence check in `deleteMerge` (1046) would read pre-shift anchors — the wrong keys and the wrong count. Today no engine path batches a shift together with a merge write (`Sheet.shiftCells` at sheet.ts:1356 runs outside its `beginBatch` at 1394), so this is latent rather than live, but the overlay silently assumes it is the only writer of `ws.merges` in a batch.

samples.summary: getMerges() does not apply the batch overlay that projectedMerges() now applies, so mid-batch reads disagree with the store's own budget view
samples.evidence: `projectedMerges()` (975-991) deliberately folds `batchMerges` over the document map, but `getMerges()` (1068-1076) still reads `ws.merges` raw. During a batch the two answer differently: `setMerge`/`deleteMerge` see queued blocks, any caller of `getMerges()` sees the pre-batch map. The only current caller is `Sheet.load` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:589), which does not run inside a batch, so this is inconsistency waiting for the next caller rather than a live wrong answer.

samples.summary: ReadOnlyStore.setMerge returning false makes the engine drop merges from its in-memory map on paste/move for read-only sheets
samples.evidence: `ReadOnlyStore.setMerge` now returns `false`. Because `applyPasteMerges` (sheet.ts:2730) and the cut/move path (sheet.ts:2977) `continue` on a falsy result, a `Sheet` backed by `ReadOnlyStore` now silently loses the moved/pasted block from `this.merges` too, and `mergeSelection` (4929) returns `false` where it previously returned `true` and merged locally. For datasource/lakehouse views (datasource-view.tsx:29, lakehouse-view.tsx:40) these commands should not be reachable, so the behavioural delta is probably desired — flagging it only because it is a semantic change to an existing no-op that no test in this delta pins down.
